newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
LEFT PARTY FLAYS GOVERNMENT POLICIES

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPM) criticised the government's policies and performance but said it had no plans to withdraw its support. Party general secretary H.S. Surjeet said the CPM politburo was concerned that the government had not fulfilled many of its promises and was deviating from the common minimum programme. He said the party could be more vigilant but was happy to give outside support to the government. The politburo was particularly critical of the finance and industry ministries' performance.
Indian Express
BOFORS DOCUMENTS TO BE HANDED OVER

Seven years after India sought Swiss assistance in the Bofors gun deal affair, secret Swiss bank documents would be transferred to the country on January 21. Sources said the controversial papers would be handed over to the Indian ambassador in Switzerland at the Swiss capital city of Berne. These papers contain details of bribes paid by Bofors for the 1986 gun deal with India.
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT CAN MANAGE TEMPLES

The Supreme Court ruled that the government was empowered to regulate Hindu places of worship to ensure their proper, efficient, effective and responsible administration. In its ruling, the court upheld the constitutionality of the Jammu and Kashmir Sri Vaishno Devi Shrine Act, 1988. The court, however, said the government could not acquire the title of the property or such religious places of worship vested in a worshipper or a religious charitable trust.
The Economic Times
PREMIER TO MEET APEX BANK CHIEF TO GALVANISE MARKET

Prime Minister H.D Deve Gowda has convened a series of high-level meetings to discuss the liquidity crunch in the industry and capital markets reforms. The first meeting is scheduled with the Reserve Bank chief to discuss the liquidity situation in the economy. The premier is also meeting the chief of Nabard, the rural development agency, for finalising fresh poverty alleviation schemes. Simultaneously, the finance secretary has called a meeting of chiefs of financial institutions on the Infrastructure Development Finance Corporation (IDFC).
ANTI MONEY LAUNDERING DRAFT BILL SEEKS DISCLOSURES

The draft recommendations on the proposed anti-money laundering law aim to make possession of unaccounted money a punishable offence. The proposed law would bar anyone from depositing large sums of money in banks without producing proof of its source. Bank officials accepting large deposits without checking the source would be liable to be fined under the proposed law. The Finance Ministry had set up a high-powered committee to draft a comprehensive anti-money laundering bill. These are the broad recommendations of the draft report of the committee on which the new anti-money laundering law would be based.
GOVERNMENT APPREHENSIVE OF BBC'S NEWS PROGRAMME

The External Affairs Ministry has expressed concern over BBC's Hindi news programme, telecast by Home TV, a local satellite television channel. Keeping in line with the government's fear of foreign media manipulating news on India, the ministry questioned whether BBC should be permitted to uplink to Home TV's earth station through VSNL, the state-owned overseas telecommunication carrier. The points of concern is BBC's editorial control over the news bulletin. Besides, the news being in Hindi, it would have higher viewership than most other channels, thus giving it a wider reach.
Financial Express
STATES FOR TRANSFER OF PROFITABLE FIRMS

The meeting of the National Development Council (NDC), called to approve the Ninth Plan approach paper, may be stormy with participants likely to rake up various contentious issues. The finalisation of the paper has already brought forth the differences among members of the United Front cabinet over the plan size, GDP growth rate and agriculture sector growth target. The issue that will figure prominently will be resource allocation. Another bone of contention would be the transfer of profitable state-owned firms to the states. This, it is argued, would help them raise resources. The meeting also assumes political overtones with the Congress expressing reservations about the paper.
RELIANCE-NYNEX REJECTS SOPS FOR SIGINING LICENCE PACT

The Reliance-Nynex venture, a letter of intent holder for the Gujarat basic services circle, has rejected concessions offered by the Department of Telecommunications for signing the licence agreement. However, four other basic service operators affirmed their willingness to sign the licence agreement, though with a few more changes. The Reliance-Nynex decision to not to accept the new conditions might emerge as another setback for the telecommunication privatisation process.
Business Standard
INSTITUTIONS TO CHECK MISUSE OF INTER-CORPORATE FUNDS

The financial institutions (FIs) have formulated guidelines on corporate governance. The new guidelines seek to impose curbs on promoters using company funds to consolidate their holdings in other group companies. The funds are usually channelled from group companies to the holding company or other companies with cross holdings to enable effective control. The need for curbs was felt after instances of FI loans being diverted to fund promoters' stake, increased.
DISINVESTMENT PLAN ON HOLD IN CURRENT FISCAL

The Industry Minister has virtually ruled out the budgeted 50 billion rupee public sector disinvestment programme in the current fiscal due to adverse market conditions. He added it was difficult to predict when the government would approach the market. The government was able to mobilise 16.8 billion rupees in the previous fiscal through public sector disinvestment, against the targeted 70 billion rupees.
PROMOTERS RAISE STAKE IN VIDEOCON FIRMS

Videocon promoters, the Dhoots, have hiked their stakes in two group companies -- Videocon International and Videocon Appliances -- through conversion of preferential warrants into equity shares. In Videocon International, the Dhoots converted five million warrants into an equal number of shares, increasing their stake from 19 to 26.15 percent. In Videocon Appliances, the other group company, the Dhoots' stake has gone up from 18 to 30.38 percent.
EXPERT GROUP ON SAVINGS CONSTITUTED

The government has constituted an expert group which would recommend measures to increase domestic savings. The group would examine the existing tax provisions for household savings and suggest a plan of action to encourage such savings in the short and medium term. The group is expected to submit its interim report by January 30 and its final report by April 30, 1997.
FOREIGN INVESTORS' REGISTRATION TO BE STREAMLINED

The Securities and Exchange Board of India, in conjunction with the Reserve Bank of India, would take steps to reduce delays in the registration procedure for foreign institutional investors (FIIs). This would include re-examining the existing requirements for FIIs' registration and the eligibility criteria of sub-accounts. The move gains significance as it becomes a definite step to further boost FII confidence and investment opportunity in the Indian markets.
The Observer
CENTRAL BANK PURVIEW TO INCLUDE MUTUAL BENEFIT SOCIETIES

The Finance Ministry is considering a proposal to bring nidhi companies (mutual benefit societies) under the jurisdiction of the Reserve bank (RBI). The move is aimed at regulating the operations of these companies through RBI guidelines for non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Ministry sources said the step sought to bring the activities of nidhis under strict scrutiny to enable the government to bring all NBFCs under a single governing law. So far, nidhis are regulated by the Department of Company Affairs.
AGRICULTURE MINISTRY TO OPPOSE WTO PRESSURE

The Agriculture Ministry will resist the government's move to commit the country to removing quantitative restrictions on import of foodgrains at world trade negotiations. A study favoured continuation of import restrictions on cereals for a fairly long time, the agriculture minister said. Being a member of the World Trade Organisation, India is under obligation to convert all quantitative restrictions on imports into tariffs. A committee has been set up to find out whether quantitative restrictions could be reimposed once they are removed and the impact of high tariff barriers on the poultry and fishing sectors.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS PUT FOOT DOWN ON ASSIGNABILITY

The financial institutions (FIs) have put assignability of licences as a precondition for sanctioning loans for telecommunication projects without corporate guarantee. The latest stand of the FIs would mount pressure on the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to hasten the process. FI sources said a waiver of corporate guarantee was possible only if DoT made the licences assignable and legalised the cut in inter-connect charges. Sources said these measures would reduce risk factor in financing telecommunication projects.
